authorship: Original house prompts written for this repository; these are not verbatim Prompt Motion prompts.
commonInstructions: Read AGENTS.md, docs/CURRENT-TASK.md, docs/REEL-PLAYBOOK.md and docs/MOTION-DIRECTION-PLAYBOOK.md before building. Follow the existing reel roadmap and local Remotion renderer.

Use only the selected recipe facts, approved copy and supplied source footage. Do not invent quantities, cooking times, nutrition, taste reactions or missing shots. Log unknowns before choosing source ranges.

Default to a faceless vertical cooking video at 1080x1920 and 30 fps, without narration. Hindi, Hinglish or English copy follows the selected audience brief; preserve Devanagari shaping and inspect fonts.
Treat palette, lettering, slogans and timings as draft creative choices. Keep the provided brand name exactly as Namak Kum Tha; no final logo, slogan or brand palette has been approved in this lab.

Keep important text within configurable house insets top 192, right 160, bottom 420, left 64 at 1080x1920, and verify the actual target app later. The configurable overlay implementation is still planned.

Cut for clear cooking actions and reading time. Music, ASMR and edit effects are optional, source-backed and subject to the current audio implementation. A declared beat grid is not measured audio synchronization.
Use project.json as the render clock. Optional direction.json only schedules review intentions. Do not pass this prompt-pack JSON to the video CLI as a render project.

Check the required capabilities against current code. When an overlay, audio layer, reaction insert, loop control or visual primitive is unavailable, record the dependency and follow the bounded roadmap rather than pretending it rendered.

Save the chosen concept, source ranges and comparison variable. Render and inspect actual opening, holds, boundaries and final frames only when testing is requested. Record structural, visual, playback, listening and phone checks separately.

Tests are deferred at the owner's request. Every experiment remains not-run until actual evidence is recorded. Do not generate a video, infer a winner or fabricate audience results merely because this pack exists.

experiments.name: Result first
experiments.prompt: Build a Namak Kum Tha recipe reel that begins with the strongest real view of the completed dish. Let that shot establish a concrete promise, then show the actions needed to achieve it in a comprehensible order. Return to a satisfying serving or texture payoff. Keep recipe facts unchanged and make each transition clarify progress. Avoid a separate animated introduction before the food. Keep a source-matched process-first alternative for comparison without changing the body edit.
experiments.hypothesis: Showing a relevant finished result early may make the recipe's purpose clearer.

experiments.name: Action first
experiments.prompt: Use a distinct physical action from the selected Namak Kum Tha footage as the first image: a pour, a fold, a cut or another clearly visible change. Select the action from actual footage rather than requesting an imaginary replacement shot. Establish what is being made with concise supported context, then reuse the agreed recipe body and payoff. Compare against result-first with equivalent duration and copy exposure. Keep the action readable before cutting away.
experiments.hypothesis: A legible action opening may create interest while preserving immediate subject recognition.

experiments.name: Texture study
experiments.prompt: Create a short Namak Kum Tha texture study from one real cooking moment. Choose a visually distinct surface or transformation and build a tiny arc: approach, contact or change, then a satisfying hold. Let the food occupy the picture. Keep labels minimal and omit a CTA if it interrupts the moment. If usable recorded sound exists, propose a listening comparison with and without it; otherwise keep the audio requirement pending rather than manufacturing an ASMR claim.
experiments.hypothesis: A focused sensory moment may communicate appeal with less explanatory text.

experiments.name: One useful technique
experiments.prompt: Make the Namak Kum Tha reel teach one useful technique that is actually demonstrated in the selected footage. Introduce the task, hold the decisive hand or utensil action long enough to follow, and show the resulting change. Supporting preparation can be compressed, but do not speed past the key evidence. Write the explanation only from the supplied recipe notes. End with the outcome rather than an unsupported claim that this technique always produces a superior result.
experiments.hypothesis: A narrower instructional promise may improve comprehension of the decisive step.

experiments.name: Ingredient spotlight
experiments.prompt: Build an ingredient-led Namak Kum Tha reel using the exact supplied ingredients and quantities. Give one important ingredient a clear visual introduction, then connect it to its actual use in the process. Prefer readable labels near a stable region of the picture over a dense full-screen list. Leave adequate exposure for longer ingredient names. Compare this presentation with the same recipe using a single ingredient card; preserve quantities, process footage and overall duration as closely as practical.
experiments.hypothesis: Contextual ingredient labels may be easier to associate with actions than a single dense list.

experiments.name: Clear step rhythm
experiments.prompt: Organize the selected Namak Kum Tha recipe around a small set of meaningful stages. Use short step labels that describe the action rather than decorating every cut with a new caption. Keep a consistent label position and hierarchy while the cooking footage changes. Place each label only when its stage begins, and preserve a clean reading hold. Do not infer cooking time from the number of seconds shown in the edited reel. Compare against the same footage with no step labels.
experiments.hypothesis: Stable stage labels may make a compressed recipe easier to follow.
reviewFocus: edited time distinguished from cooking time

experiments.name: Match the action
experiments.prompt: Find two real Namak Kum Tha shots with compatible direction, shape or hand movement. Connect them with a direct cut that makes the action feel related without concealing a necessary recipe step. Use crop and focus to support the relationship while keeping the food identifiable. If no useful match exists, state that finding and choose a clear editorial cut. Compare against a conventional cut between the same moments; do not add a synthetic transition solely to manufacture continuity.
experiments.hypothesis: A purposeful action match may make a short sequence feel more connected.

experiments.name: Deliberate pause
experiments.prompt: Take the agreed Namak Kum Tha recipe cut and give its most useful visual payoff a longer uninterrupted hold. Choose a moment whose information benefits from time, such as a texture reveal or an observable technique result. Recover the required duration by reducing repetition elsewhere rather than deleting a necessary instruction. Compare with the original pacing at the same overall length. Keep the hold purposeful; do not call an unexplained freeze or an empty frame a cinematic pause.
experiments.hypothesis: Redistributing time toward a meaningful payoff may improve understanding or satisfaction.

experiments.name: Food before branding
experiments.prompt: Introduce Namak Kum Tha through a real cooking image before displaying the channel name. Add the name only where it supports recognition without obscuring the food or delaying the first meaningful action. Keep any end identification brief and readable. Compare with the same clip carrying a small early brand label. Do not design a final logo or adopt a permanent slogan in this experiment; use editable text and retain the supplied spelling exactly.
experiments.hypothesis: Putting the subject first may preserve opening clarity while still establishing the channel identity.

experiments.name: Restraint in type
experiments.prompt: Use the agreed Namak Kum Tha footage and facts to build a restrained text treatment. Reserve the largest type for the single most useful message, use a supporting size for steps, and reduce decorative microcopy. Keep a stable alignment and inspect the longest line at phone scale. Compare with a denser text treatment using the same information and timing. Remove redundant wording before shrinking type, while preserving every necessary quantity and instruction.
experiments.hypothesis: A clearer type hierarchy may improve reading order without increasing caption exposure.

experiments.name: Hindi and Hinglish comparison
experiments.prompt: Prepare two readable text treatments for the same Namak Kum Tha recipe: the selected Hindi wording in Devanagari and its reviewed Hinglish equivalent. Keep the facts, footage and narrative order stable. Fit each version naturally rather than forcing identical line breaks. Check conjuncts, vowel marks, mixed numerals and the longest ingredient name. Treat linguistic equivalence as a review task. Do not infer which script the audience prefers from the cuisine or declare a winner before testing.
experiments.hypothesis: Audience comprehension may differ by script; preference must be observed rather than assumed.

experiments.name: Sound-led cooking moment
experiments.prompt: Choose a Namak Kum Tha moment with an actual useful recorded sound, inspect its onset and pair it with the visible action that produced it. Give that sound space in the mix if the audio-layer feature is available. Keep the same short sequence understandable when muted. Compare the source-sound version with a reviewed music-led version only after both mixes exist. Do not double the same sound across layers or label unrelated stock audio as the original recording.
experiments.hypothesis: Accurate sound-action alignment may strengthen a sensory moment while preserving muted clarity.

experiments.name: Selective beat accents
experiments.prompt: Use a supplied cleared track and mark a small number of meaningful musical events before editing this Namak Kum Tha variant. Align selected reveals or major cuts where the action still reads clearly. Leave useful technique holds independent of the beat. Record the track offset, measured or manually checked markers and intentional off-grid edits. Compare against the same narrative cut without beat adjustment. A generic 120 BPM planning grid is insufficient evidence that this experiment is synchronized.
experiments.hypothesis: Selective musical emphasis may support rhythm without sacrificing instructional clarity.

experiments.name: Complete mini-story
experiments.prompt: Create a Namak Kum Tha mini-story from one real setup, one meaningful change and one payoff found in the selected footage. Keep it understandable without narration. If a joke is proposed, make it depend on the observed situation rather than an invented failure, reaction or recipe claim. Use concise text only where the images need context. End after the payoff lands. An optional reaction accent must remain secondary to the creator's own cooking footage and requires the planned insert support.
experiments.hypothesis: A complete small narrative may work more clearly than a collection of unrelated quick shots.

experiments.name: Real correction
experiments.prompt: If the selected Namak Kum Tha material contains a real mistake or useful correction, explain that specific event with its visible evidence and resolution. Distinguish an observed occurrence from a general cooking rule. Keep the corrective action readable and preserve any recipe context needed to interpret it. If the source material contains no correction, mark this concept unsuitable and select another experiment. Do not stage a false disaster or invent a warning to create tension.
experiments.hypothesis: An evidenced correction may provide a useful narrative question when the source material supports one.

experiments.name: Natural return
experiments.prompt: Look for a naturally repeatable motion in Namak Kum Tha footage and assess whether an ending can return smoothly to the opening. Preserve a complete payoff and avoid creating an extra pause by duplicating the endpoint. Inspect the wrap for direction, speed, crop, text and sound. If the source motion cannot support a convincing return, retain a clear ending and record why. Compare looping and non-looping treatments without assuming that an additional rewatch means better comprehension.
experiments.hypothesis: A natural return may feel satisfying when it preserves the action and payoff.

experiments.name: Quiet recipe card
experiments.prompt: Add one clearly readable recipe-reference moment to the agreed Namak Kum Tha reel. Include only reviewed information that a viewer may need to revisit. Size the information for the target phone and reserve enough reading exposure; split the card if necessary. Keep the complete cooking payoff before an optional viewer action. Compare the card treatment with contextual ingredient labels while retaining the same factual content. Do not compress an entire recipe into unreadably small type to claim it is saveable.
experiments.hypothesis: A usable reference moment may improve practical utility when the information remains readable.

experiments.name: One restrained invitation
experiments.prompt: Prepare two endings for the same Namak Kum Tha reel after its real payoff is complete. One ends on the food; the other adds a single light invitation appropriate to the actual value delivered, such as revisiting the recipe or sharing a relatable moment. Keep the rest of the video stable. Do not stack follow, comment, save and share instructions or invent social proof. Make the optional line readable without obscuring the final dish.
experiments.hypothesis: A relevant, restrained invitation may help viewers act without weakening the payoff.
requiredCapabilities: optional text overlay or end card

experiments.name: One visual motif
experiments.prompt: Develop one small original visual motif for the selected Namak Kum Tha recipe, derived from an actual object, shape or process in that recipe. Reuse it sparingly to connect a stage label with the payoff while keeping cooking footage dominant. Explain what the motif communicates before building it. Start with one representative scene and inspect it. If the effect needs a new primitive, implement it only after its value and two concrete uses are clear; do not introduce a separate animation stack.
experiments.hypothesis: A meaningful recurring motif may improve continuity without adding unrelated decoration.

experiments.name: Same recipe, three directions
experiments.prompt: Using the same reviewed Namak Kum Tha recipe and source footage, propose three distinct treatments: clear instructional, tactile sensory, and a concise situation-led story where the footage supports one. State what each treatment prioritizes and what tradeoffs it makes. Build only when testing is requested, keeping factual content and source provenance consistent. This is creative exploration with multiple changing variables, not a controlled single-variable experiment. Select a direction from actual comprehension and viewing evidence, then isolate narrower variables in later comparisons.
experiments.hypothesis: A broader direction comparison may identify a promising editorial approach before narrow experiments.
reviewFocus: no causal claim from multi-variable comparison
